Sauce for Slices: chop hard eggs, pepper, cumin, parsley, a little costmary, a myrtle berry, rather more honey, vinegar, fish-sauce, oil.
Raw Dill-Sauce for Boiled Meat: pepper, dill seed, dry mint, laser root, moisten with vinegar, add dates, honey, fish-sauce, a little mustard, oil, temper with reduced must, and proceed to give it colour.
Fish-Pickle Sauce for Boiled Meat: pepper, lovage, caraway, celery seed, thyme, onion, date, strained fish-pickle, honey, and wine, temper. Scatter chopped green celery over the top. Put in oil and serve.
Stomachs. Empty a pig's stomach well, with vinegar and salt, then wash it with water, and so fill it with this stuffing: pork flesh pounded and ground, and so de-nerved, mixed with three brains and raw eggs, into which you pour pine kernels and put whole pepper, and temper with this sauce: pound pepper, lovage, silphium, anise, ginger, a little rue, the best fish-sauce, and a little oil. Fill the belly so that it has slack, lest it burst in the cooking. Pin both ends and plunge it into a boiling pot. Lift it and prick it with a needle so that it does not crack. When it is cooked halfway, wash it and hang it in the smoke so that it takes colour. And again boil it thoroughly so that it can be cooked; then with fish-sauce, unmixed wine, a little oil. And you will open it with a knife and serve it with fish-sauce and lovage.
To Make a Stomach as Though Roasted, wrap it in bran, then put it into brine, and so cook it.
Roasted Loins are made thus: they are opened into two parts, so that they are spread out, and ground pepper is scattered over them, pine kernels and coriander chopped very fine and ground fennel seed; then the loins are closed up spread out, sewn together, and wrapped in caul, and so seared in oil and fish-sauce; thence they are roasted in an oven or on a gridiron.
A Ham, when you have boiled it with many dried figs and three bay leaves, with the skin drawn off, cut it crosswise and fill it with honey; then weave a paste of flour kneaded with oil and restore its skin to it. And when the paste is cooked, take it from the oven, just as it is, and serve.
The Cooking of a Ham: cooked plainly from water with dried figs, as is usual, served with morsels, boiled must or spiced wine — better still with the juice of must-cakes.
Fore-ham with Must-Cakes: boil the fore-ham with two pounds of barley and twenty-five dried figs. When it is boiled, cut off the rind and burn its edge with a glowing iron and touch it with honey. Better still, put in the oven, smear it with honey. When it has taken colour, put into a pot raisin-wine, pepper, a bundle of rue, unmixed wine, temper. When it is tempered, pour half over the fore-ham, and with the other part of the peppered sauce drench the morsels of must-cake set ready. When they have sucked it up, whatever the must-cakes refuse, pour back over the fore-ham.

title: De Re Coquinaria
text:
The Cooking of Bacon: cooked covered with water and much dill, drip on a little oil and a little salt.
Kid's or Lamb's Liver you will cook thus: make honey-water and eggs, mix in part milk, so that the cut liver may soak it up. Cook it and serve with wine-and-fish-sauce, with pepper scattered.
Otherwise, with Lungs: wash the lungs in milk — and strain off what they can take up — and break in two raw eggs, a few grains of salt, a spoonful of honey, and mix in fine flour, and fill the lungs, boil them, and chop them.
Pound pepper, moisten with fish-sauce, raisin-wine, unmixed wine. Prick the lungs and pour this wine-and-fish-sauce over them.
Homely Sweets: small palm-dates or dates, stoned, with a nut or pine kernels, honey, ground pepper. Stuff them, touch them outside with salt. Fry in cooked honey and serve.
Otherwise, Sweets: scrape the best African must-cakes and steep them in milk. When they have drunk it up, put them in the oven. So that they do not dry out, take them out a little. While they are hot, pour honey over them, prick them so that they drink it up. Scatter pepper and serve.
Otherwise, Sweets: scrape fine-wheat cakes, make larger morsels, soak them in milk, fry them in oil. Pour honey over them and serve.
Sweets: into the peppered mixture put honey, unmixed wine, raisin-wine, rue; into this put pine kernels, mix boiled spelt-grits, chopped walnuts, add roasted hazelnuts, and serve.
Otherwise, Sweets: pound pepper, pine kernels, honey, rue, and raisin-wine, with milk and a pasta sheet; bring it to a curd, cook it doused with a few eggs, scatter honey over it, and serve.
Otherwise, Sweets: take fine flour, cook it in hot water, so that you make a very stiff porridge. Then spread it on a board. When it has cooled, cut it as for sweets, and fry it in the best oil. Lift it, pour honey over it. Scatter pepper and serve. You will do better if you put milk instead of water.
Tripatina: take milk, judge it against the size of the dish, temper the milk with honey as for milk-puddings, put in five eggs to a pint, or, if to a half-pint, three eggs. Dissolve them in the milk so that you make a single body. Set it in a Cumaean dish and cook over a slow fire. When it has drawn together, scatter pepper and serve.
Egg Sponge with Milk: four eggs, a half-pint of milk, an ounce of oil, dissolve together so that you make a single body. Add a little oil to a thin pan, make it boil, and add the mixture you have prepared. When it is cooked on one side, turn it onto a dish, pour honey over it, scatter pepper, and serve.
Curds: sour milk, pepper and fish-sauce, honey, salt, oil, and coriander.
Bulbs with oil, fish-sauce, vinegar. Serve with a little cumin scattered. Otherwise: pour out the bulbs, cook them in equal water, then fry in oil. Make the sauce thus: thyme, pennyroyal, pepper, oregano, honey, a little vinegar, and, if you like, a little fish-sauce. Scatter pepper and serve.
Otherwise: boil the bulbs, press them in a saucepan, put in thyme, oregano, honey, vinegar, reduced must, date, fish-sauce, and a little oil. Scatter pepper and serve.
Otherwise: fried bulbs you will serve with wine-and-fish-sauce.
Cornel-Mushrooms: boiled and hot, dried, are taken with wine-and-fish-sauce and pepper, so that you grind the pepper with fish-sauce.
For Cornel-Mushrooms: pepper, boiled must, vinegar, and oil.
Otherwise, Cornel-Mushrooms boiled are served with salt, oil, unmixed wine, and chopped coriander.
Boletus Mushrooms: pour over them boiled must, a bundle of green coriander. When it has boiled, take out the bundle and serve.

title: De Re Coquinaria
text:
Boletus Mushrooms, Otherwise: their stalks scattered with fish-sauce or salt they serve.
Boletus Mushrooms, Otherwise: their stems cut up, into a pan. Pour over them grape-juice, with pepper added, lovage, a little honey, temper with fish-sauce. A little oil.
Truffles: scrape them, boil them, scatter salt, fix them on a skewer, and roast them lightly; then put into a pot oil, fish-sauce, boiled must, wine, pepper, and honey. When it has boiled, bind with starch. Unload the truffles and serve.
Otherwise, Truffles: boil them, and with salt scattered fix them on skewers and roast them lightly, and put into a pot fish-sauce, green oil, boiled must, a little wine, broken pepper, and a little honey, and let it boil. When it has boiled, bind with starch and prick the truffles so that they drink it up. Unload them. When they have well sucked it up, serve. If you wish, wrap these same truffles in pork caul and roast them, and so serve.
Otherwise, Truffles with Wine-and-Fish-Sauce: pepper, lovage, coriander, rue, fish-sauce, honey, wine, a little oil. Heat it.
Otherwise, Truffles: pepper, mint, rue, honey, oil, a little wine. Heat it and serve.
Otherwise: boil truffles with leek, then salt, pepper, chopped coriander, the best unmixed wine. Serve.
Otherwise, Truffles: pepper, cumin, hartwort, mint, celery, rue, honey, vinegar or wine, salt or fish-sauce, and a little oil.
For Taro: pepper, cumin, rue, honey, fish-sauce, a little oil. When it has boiled, bind with starch.
Snails: take snails, sponge them, take off the membrane so that they can come out. Put into a vessel milk and salt for one day, on the other days milk alone, and clear off the dung every hour. When they are fattened, so that they cannot draw back, fry them in oil, put on wine-and-fish-sauce. Likewise they can be fed with reduced must from the flesh.
Roast snails with pure salt and oil. Roast Snails: laser, fish-sauce, pepper, oil. Pour over. Roast Snails: fish-sauce, pepper, cumin, oil. Pour over constantly.
Otherwise, Snails: soak living snails in fine-wheat milk. When they are fattened, cook them.
Eggs Fried in Wine-and-Fish-Sauce: boiled eggs with fish-sauce, oil, unmixed wine; or with fish-sauce, pepper, laser. In Soft-Boiled Eggs: pepper, lovage, soaked pine kernels, moisten with honey, vinegar, temper with fish-sauce.
Here begins the Four-Footed Book of Apicius Caelius.
VIII.
Wild Boar is seasoned thus: it is sponged and so salt is scattered on it, and roasted cumin, and so it stands. The next day it is put into the oven. When it is cooked, it is poured over with ground pepper, honey, fish-sauce, boiled must, and raisin-wine.
Otherwise, for Wild Boar: boil the boar in sea-water with bay twigs until it is steeped. Take off its skin. Serve it with salt, mustard, vinegar.
Otherwise, for Wild Boar: pound pepper, lovage, oregano, softened myrtle berries, coriander, onions, moisten with honey, wine, fish-sauce, a little oil. Heat it, bind with starch. Pour over the boar cooked in the oven. You will do this also for every kind of game meat.
For Roasted Boar you will make hot sauces thus: pepper, roasted cumin, celery seed, mint, thyme, savory, safflower flowers, roasted pine kernels or roasted almonds, honey, wine, a cup of fish-sauce, a little oil.
Otherwise, Hot Sauces for Roasted Boar: pepper, lovage, celery seed, mint, thyme, roasted pine kernels, wine, vinegar, fish-sauce, and a little oil. When the plain sauce has boiled, then put in a ball of the ground mixture and stir with a bundle of onion and rue. If you wish to make it richer, bind, if you like, with the liquid white of eggs. Move it gently. Scatter ground pepper and serve.

title: De Re Coquinaria
text:
Sauce for Boiled Boar: pepper, lovage, cumin, hartwort, oregano, pine kernels, date, mustard, vinegar, fish-sauce, and oil.
Cold Sauce for Boiled Boar: pepper, caraway, lovage, roasted coriander seed, dill seed, celery seed, thyme, oregano, onion, honey, vinegar, mustard, fish-sauce, oil.
Otherwise, Cold Sauce for Boiled Boar: pepper, lovage, cumin, dill seed and thyme, oregano, a little hartwort, rather more rocket seed, moisten with unmixed wine, green seasonings, a little onion, fried hazelnut or almond, date, honey, vinegar, a little unmixed wine, give it colour with reduced must, fish-sauce, oil.
Otherwise, Sauce for Boar: pound pepper, lovage, oregano, celery seed, laser root, cumin, fennel seed, rue, fish-sauce, wine, raisin-wine. Make it boil. When it has boiled, bind with starch. Touch the boar inside and out and serve.
A Boar's Ham is stuffed Terentine-style thus: through the joint of the ham put a stake so that you separate the skin from the flesh, so that it can take seasoning through a little horn and be wholly filled. Pound pepper, a bay berry, rue; if you wish, add laser; the best fish-sauce, boiled must, and drops of green oil.
When it is filled, that part by which it was filled is bound with linen, and it is put into broth and boiled in sea-water with bay-shoots and dill.
Sauce for Venison: pound pepper, lovage, caraway, oregano, celery seed, laser root, fennel seed, work it, moisten with fish-sauce, wine, raisin-wine, a little oil. When it has boiled, bind with starch. Touch the cooked venison inside and out and serve.
For roebuck likewise, and for every kind of game you use the same seasoning.
Otherwise, boil the venison and roast it lightly. Pound pepper, lovage, caraway, celery seed, moisten with honey, vinegar, fish-sauce, oil. Heated, bind with starch and pour over the meat.
Sauce for Venison: pepper, lovage, onion, oregano, pine kernels, dates, honey, fish-sauce, mustard, vinegar, oil.
Seasoning for Venison: pepper, cumin, condiment, onion, rue, mint, honey, fish-sauce, raisin-wine, boiled must, and a little oil. Bind with starch when it is already boiling.
Hot Sauces for Venison: pepper, lovage, parsley, cumin, moisten, roasted pine kernels or almonds, honey, vinegar, wine, a little oil, fish-sauce, and stir the sauce.
For Roasted Venison: pepper, Indian spikenard, spikenard leaf, celery seed, dried onion, green rue, honey, vinegar, fish-sauce, with dates added, raisins, and oil.
Otherwise, for Roasted Venison, Hot Sauces: pepper, lovage, parsley, softened damsons, wine, honey, vinegar, fish-sauce, a little oil. Stir with leek and savory.
Sauce for Roebuck: pepper, lovage, caraway, cumin, parsley, rue seed, honey, mustard, vinegar, fish-sauce, and oil.
Sauce for Roasted Roebuck: pepper, condiment, rue, onion, honey, fish-sauce, raisin-wine, a little oil, starch when it is already boiling.
Otherwise, Sauce for Roebuck: pepper, condiment, a little oregano, rue, fish-sauce, honey, raisin-wine, and a little oil, bind with starch.
Hot Sauce for Mouflon: pepper, lovage, cumin, dry mint, thyme, silphium, moisten with wine, add softened damsons, honey, wine, fish-sauce, vinegar, raisin-wine for colour, oil; stir with a bundle of oregano and dry mint.
Sauce for All Game, Boiled and Roasted: of pepper eight scruples, rue, lovage, celery seed, juniper, thyme, dry mint, six scruples each, of pennyroyal three scruples. Reduce all these to a very fine powder, mix them into one, and grind them. Add into a little vessel as much honey as is enough. And use them with vinegar-sauce.

title: De Re Coquinaria
text:
Cold Sauce for Mouflon: pepper, lovage, thyme, roasted cumin, roasted pine kernels, honey, vinegar, fish-sauce, and oil. Scatter pepper.
Fried Veal: pepper, lovage, celery seed, cumin, oregano, dried onion, raisins, honey, vinegar, wine, fish-sauce, oil, reduced must.
Veal or Beef with leeks, spring onions, or taro, fish-sauce, pepper, laser, and a little oil.
For Boiled Veal: pound pepper, lovage, caraway, celery seed, moisten with honey, vinegar, fish-sauce, oil. Heat it, bind with starch, and pour over the meat.
Otherwise, for Boiled Veal: pepper, lovage, fennel seed, oregano, pine kernels, dates, honey, vinegar, fish-sauce, mustard, and oil.
Slices of Kid or Lamb: cook with pepper and fish-sauce, with spelt-bean stew, fish-sauce, pepper, laser, with morsels of bread soaked in gravy and a little oil.
Otherwise, Stewed Kid or Lamb: put the slices into a pot. Cut onion and coriander small. Pound pepper, lovage, cumin, fish-sauce, oil, wine. Cook. Empty into a dish, bind with starch.
Otherwise, Stewed Kid or Lamb: raw lamb ought to take the ground mortar-mixture, but goat takes the ground mixture when it is being cooked.
Roasted Kid or Lamb: when you have cooked it in fish-sauce and oil, soak it cut up in pepper, laser, fish-sauce, a little oil, and roast it on a gridiron. Touch it with the same sauce. Scatter pepper and serve.
Otherwise, Roasted Kid or Lamb: of pepper half an ounce, of asarum six scruples, a little ginger, of parsley six scruples, a little laser, of the best fish-sauce a half-pint, of oil a cup.
Kid or Lamb Syringian Style, that is, Suckling: it is carefully boned from the throat, so that it becomes a bag and its entrails are emptied whole, so that air is blown into the entrails by way of the head and the dung is emptied from the hindmost part. They are washed carefully with water. And so they are filled, with fish-sauce mixed in, and on account of the moisture it is sewn up and put into the oven. When it is cooked, a boiling sauce is poured over: milk, ground pepper, fish-sauce, boiled must, a little reduced must, so also oil, and to the already boiling sauce you add starch. Or at least it is put into a net or a little basket and carefully bound, and plunged into boiling broth with a little salt. When it has boiled there well, through three surgings, it is lifted, and again it boils with the moisture written above. With the boiling seasoning it is poured over.
Otherwise, Syringian Kid or Lamb: of milk one pint, of honey four ounces, of pepper one ounce, a little salt, a little laser. Its own sauce: a cup of oil, a cup of fish-sauce, a cup of honey, eight pounded dates, a half-pint of good wine, a little starch.
Raw Kid or Lamb: rub it with oil and pepper, and scatter pure salt outside with much coriander seed. Put it into the oven. Serve it roasted.
Tarpeian Kid or Lamb: before it is cooked, dressed, it is sewn up. Pepper, rue, savory, onion, a little thyme, and fish-sauce. Wash the kid, soften it in the oven or in a pan that has oil. When it is cooked through, pour over it in the pan this stuffing: pound savory, onion, rue, dates, wine, boiled must, oil. When it has well taken up the stuffing, set it on a dish, scatter pepper, and serve.
Parthian Kid or Lamb: put it into the oven. Pound pepper, rue, onion, savory, stoned damsons, a little fresh laser, fish-sauce, and wine. It is washed boiling-hot on a dish; it is taken with vinegar.
Bay-Leaf Kid in Milk: dress the kid, bone it, take out its inwards with the rennet, wash it. Put into a mortar pepper, lovage, laser root, two bay berries, a little pellitory, two or three brains. Pound all these, moisten with fish-sauce, temper with salt. Over the ground mixture strain two pints of milk, two spoonfuls of honey. With this stuffing fill the entrails and arrange them in a ring over the kid, and cover with caul and paper, pin it. Set the kid in a pot or pan, add fish-sauce, oil, wine. When it has come to the middle of cooking, pound pepper, lovage, and moisten with its own juice, put in a little reduced must, pound, empty into the casing. When it is cooked through, unload it, bind with starch, and serve.

title: De Re Coquinaria
text:
Plain Lamb: of a skinned lamb make slices, wash them, put them carefully into a pot, add oil, fish-sauce, wine, leek, coriander cut with a knife. When it begins to boil, stir the sauce with an onion and serve.
Laser Kid: with the entrails of the kid well cleaned, stuff them with pepper, fish-sauce, laser, oil, and put them inside the kid, sew it well, and they are cooked together with the kid. And when it is cooked through, put into a mortar rue, a bay berry, and with the kid lifted and dried, pour its own sauce over it, and so set it down.
Stuffed Sucking-Pig in Two Ways: dress it, gut it from the throat, prepare it. Before you sear it, open the little ear carefully, put the Terentine stuffing into a bull's bladder, then tie the reed of a bird-feeder to the mouth of the bladder, through which you press into the ear as much as it can take, then close it with paper and pin it. And prepare another stuffing thus: pound pepper, lovage, oregano, a little laser root, moisten with fish-sauce, add cooked brains, raw eggs, boiled spelt-grits, its own juice, and, if there are any, small birds, pine kernels, whole pepper, temper with fish-sauce. Fill the sucking-pig, cover it with paper and pins. Put it into the oven. When it is cooked, unload it, grease it, and serve.
Otherwise, Sucking-Pig: salt, cumin, laser. Take out the inner bag of the fish-sauced pig, so that some flesh remains in it. Pound pepper, lovage, oregano, moisten with fish-sauce, add one brain, two eggs. Mix together. Fill the seared sucking-pig, pin it. Plunge it in a little basket into a boiling pot. When cooked, take off the pins so that the sauce can drain from it. Serve with pepper scattered.
Stuffed Boiled Sucking-Pig: take out the inner bag of the sucking-pig, sear it. Pound pepper, lovage, oregano, moisten with fish-sauce, cooked brains as much as is enough, likewise dissolve eggs, temper with fish-sauce. Cut up whole cooked sausages, but first wash the seared sucking-pig with fish-sauce, then fill it, pin it, plunge it in a little basket into a boiling pot. When cooked, sponge it, and serve without pepper.
Roasted Sucking-Pig with Pasta-and-Honey: dress the sucking-pig, gut it from the throat, dry it. Pound an ounce of pepper, honey, wine. Set it to boil. Break the dried pasta sheet and mix it in pieces into a pot, stir with a sprig of green bay, cook it so long until it becomes smooth and grows thick. With this stuffing fill the sucking-pig, pin it, cover it with paper, put it in the oven. Garnish and serve.
Milk-Fed Sucking-Pig, Boiled, Hot, with Raw Apician Sauce: put into a mortar pepper, lovage, coriander seed, mint, rue, work it, moisten with fish-sauce, add honey, wine, and fish-sauce, and pour it over the boiling boiled sucking-pig dried with a clean cloth, and serve.
Vitellian Sucking-Pig: dress the sucking-pig like a boar, scatter salt, roast it in the oven. Put into a mortar pepper, lovage, moisten with fish-sauce, temper with wine and raisin-wine. Into a pot a little oil. Let it boil. And sprinkle the roasted sucking-pig with the sauce, so that it takes it up under the skin.
Flaccian Sucking-Pig: dress the sucking-pig in the manner of a boar, scatter salt, and put it into the oven. While it cooks, put into a mortar pepper, lovage, caraway, celery seed, laser root, green rue, work it, moisten with fish-sauce, temper with wine and raisin-wine. Into a pot a little oil. Let it boil, bind with starch. Touch the cooked sucking-pig at the bones — grind celery seed so that it becomes a powder — scatter it, and serve.

title: De Re Coquinaria
text:
Bay-Crowned Sucking-Pig: bone the sucking-pig, dress it as for wine-and-fish-sauce, sear it. Break enough green bay into the middle of it. Into the oven, roast it. And put into a mortar pepper, lovage, caraway, celery seed, laser root, bay berries, work it, moisten with fish-sauce, and temper with wine and raisin-wine. Add a little oil into a pot and let it boil. Bind it. Take the sucking-pig from the bay, touch the sauce at the bone, and serve.
Frontonian Sucking-Pig: bone it, sear it, dress it. Put into a pot fish-sauce, wine, tie a bundle of leek, dill, halfway through cooking put in reduced must. When cooked, wash it and set it dry. Scatter pepper and serve.
Sucking-Pig Cooked in a Cauldron: sear the sucking-pig, dress it, add into a pot oil, fish-sauce, wine, water, tie a bundle of leek, coriander, halfway through cooking give it colour with reduced must. Put into a mortar pepper, lovage, caraway, oregano, celery seed, laser root, work it, moisten with fish-sauce, its own juice, temper with wine and raisin-wine. Empty into the pot, make it boil. When it has boiled, bind with starch. Pour over the sucking-pig set in a pan, scatter pepper, and serve.
Celsinian Sucking-Pig: dress it, pour in pepper, rue, onion, savory, cucumber juice, and pour eggs in through the ear. And from pepper, fish-sauce, a little wine. Temper in a small cup and take it.
Roasted Sucking-Pig: pound pepper, rue, savory, onion, the middles of cooked eggs, fish-sauce, wine, oil, spiced wine. Let it boil. Pour the seasoning over the sucking-pig in a serving-dish and serve.
Granary Sucking-Pig: the sucking-pig is boned, through the throat in the manner of a wineskin. There is put into it a forcemeat chicken cut into little pieces, thrushes, fig-peckers, forcemeats of its own flesh, Lucanian sausages, stoned dates, smiths' bulbs, shelled snails, mallows, beets, leeks, celery, boiled cabbage-shoots, coriander, whole pepper, pine kernels; fifteen eggs are poured over, peppered fish-sauce, grapes are put in. It is tied up and sewn together and seared, roasted in the oven. Then it is split along the back and poured over with this sauce: pound pepper, rue, fish-sauce, raisin-wine, honey, a little oil. When it has boiled, starch is put in.
Cold Sauce for an Unboiled Sucking-Pig you will make thus: pound pepper, caraway, dill, a little oregano, pine kernels, moisten with vinegar, fish-sauce, date, honey, prepared mustard, drip oil over the top, scatter pepper, and serve.
Salt-Cured Sucking-Pig you will make thus: bone the sucking-pig and prepare it as for the one cooked in a cauldron, and hang it in the smoke, but weigh it, and put in as much salt as it weighs. Put it into a pot and boil it so that it cooks, and so bring it out on a platter with fresh salt-fish.
For a Milk-Fed Sucking-Pig: of pepper one ounce, of wine a half-pint, of the best oil a cup, of vinegar a smaller cup.
Coriander Sucking-Pig: roast the sucking-pig carefully. Make a dry mortar in which you pound pepper, dill, oregano; mix in green coriander, honey, wine, fish-sauce, oil, vinegar, reduced must. Pour all these, heated, over it, and scatter raisins, pine kernels, and chopped onion, and so serve.
Sucking-Pig Cooked in a Cauldron: take a sucking-pig, dress it, cook it in oil and fish-sauce. While it cooks, put into a mortar pepper, rue, a bay berry, fish-sauce, raisin-wine or boiled must, old wine, pound all together, temper, and transfer into a bronze pan. Put it in.
Sucking-Pig in the Same Sauce: cook it through. But when you lift it, bind with starch, and so transfer it into a vessel and serve.

title: De Re Coquinaria
text:
Sucking-Pig Sprinkled with Thyme: boil a milk-fed sucking-pig killed the day before, with salt and dill, and dip it constantly in cold water so that it has whiteness. Then green seasonings, thyme, a little pennyroyal, hard eggs, onion chopped small, scatter all these over it and season with a half-pint of fish-sauce, a pound of oil, a pound of raisin-wine, and so serve.
Sharp-Broth Sucking-Pig: dress a well-prepared sucking-pig and put it into broth seasoned thus: put into a mortar fifty grains of pepper, as much honey as is fitting, three dried onions, a little green or dried coriander, a half-pint of fish-sauce, an ounce of oil, a half-pint of water; temper together in a little pot. Put the sucking-pig in it. When it begins to boil, stir the sauce with an onion so that it becomes thick. If it begins to make somewhat less sauce, then add a half-pint of water. Cook it through thus, and so serve the sucking-pig.
Laser Sucking-Pig: pound in a mortar pepper, lovage, caraway, mix in a little cumin, fresh laser, moisten with vinegar, add pine kernels, date, honey, vinegar, fish-sauce, prepared mustard. Temper all with oil and pour over.
Broth-Sauced Sucking-Pig: put into a mortar pepper, lovage or dill, coriander, rue, a bay berry, work it, moisten with fish-sauce, with leek, a little raisin-wine or honey, a little wine, some oil. When you have cooked it, bind with starch.
Sour Hare: it is parboiled a little in water, then arranged in a pan to be cooked in oil in the oven, and when it is nearly cooked, in fresh oil, touch it with the seasoning written below: pound pepper, savory, onion, rue, celery seed, fish-sauce, laser, wine, and a little oil. It is turned several times; it is cooked through in the seasoning itself.
Likewise another stuffing for it, when it is nearly to be taken off: pound pepper, date, laser, raisins, boiled must, fish-sauce, oil. Moisten, and when it has boiled, scatter pepper and serve.
Stuffed Hare: whole pine kernels, almonds, chopped walnuts or acorns, solid grains of pepper, flesh of the hare itself, and it is bound with broken eggs. It is covered with pork caul. Into the oven. So you will make the stuffing again: rue, pepper, savory, onion, savory, date, laser, fish-sauce, boiled must, or spiced wine. Let it boil together a long time until it thickens, and so it is poured over. But let the hare remain in peppered fish-sauce and laser.
White Sauce for Roasted Hare: pepper, lovage, cumin, celery seed, the middle of a hard egg. Gather the ground mixture and make a ball of it on the outside. In a little pot cook fish-sauce, wine, oil, vinegar, a little chopped onion; then put in the little ball of seasoning and stir with oregano or savory; if there is need, bind with starch.
Otherwise, Hare: a hash of hare's blood and liver and lungs. Put into a pot fish-sauce and oil; in the cooking chop leek and coriander small, put it into the pot. When they are cooked, pound pepper, cumin, coriander, laser root, mint, rue, pennyroyal, moisten with vinegar, add the hare's liver and blood, pound, temper with honey and its own juice, vinegar. Empty into the pot, put the hare's lungs chopped small into the same pot. Make it boil. When it has boiled, bind with starch, scatter pepper, and serve.
Otherwise, Hare in its Own Juice: dress the hare, bone it, prepare it, put it into a pot, add fish-sauce with oil, in the cooking a bundle of leek, coriander, dill. While it cooks, put into a mortar pepper, lovage, cumin, coriander seed, laser root, dried onion, mint, rue, celery seed, work it, moisten with fish-sauce, add rather more of its own juice, temper with reduced must, vinegar. Make it boil; when it has boiled, bind with starch. Garnish, pour the sauce over, scatter pepper, and serve.

title: De Re Coquinaria
text:
Passenian Hare: dress the hare, bone it, prepare it stretched out, hang it in the smoke. When it has taken colour, make it cook halfway. Wash it, scatter a lump of salt. Touch it with wine-and-fish-sauce: put into a mortar pepper, lovage, work it, moisten with fish-sauce, temper with wine and fish-sauce. Into a pot, add a little oil, make it boil. When it has boiled, bind with starch. Touch the roasted hare along the back, scatter pepper, and serve.
Forcemeat Hare: with the same cooking season the flesh, mix in soaked pine kernels, cover it with caul or gather the slices with paper and skewers.
Stuffed Hare: dress the hare, prepare it, set it square. Put into a mortar pepper, lovage, oregano, moisten with fish-sauce. Add cooked chicken livers, cooked brains, chopped flesh, three raw eggs, temper with fish-sauce. Cover with caul and paper and pin it. Roast it lightly over a slow fire. Put into a mortar pepper, lovage, work it, moisten with fish-sauce, temper with wine and fish-sauce. Make it boil. When it has boiled, bind with starch and pour over the lightly roasted hare. Scatter pepper and serve.
Hare, Boiled Otherwise: dress it, add onto a platter oil, fish-sauce, vinegar, raisin-wine, chop onion and green rue, thyme sliced under, and so set it out.
Pound pepper, rue, onion, the liver of the hare, fish-sauce, boiled must, raisin-wine, a little oil, starch when it boils.
Hare Sprinkled Dry. This too you season beforehand like the Tarpeian kid; before it is cooked, dressed, it is sewn up. Pepper, rue, savory, onion, a little thyme, wash it with fish-sauce, then cook it in the oven and scatter around it this stuffing: half an ounce of pepper, rue, onion, savory, four dates, a fair amount of raisins. Heat it over a fire-pan. Wine, oil, fish-sauce, boiled must. It is touched frequently so that it takes up all its seasoning. Then with pepper, dry, on a dish. It is taken.
Otherwise, Seasoned Hare: cook it in wine, fish-sauce, water. A little mustard, dill, leek with its hair on. When it has cooked in itself, season it: pepper, savory, round onion, dates, two damsons, wine, fish-sauce, boiled must, a little oil, let it be bound with starch. Let it boil a little. The hare is poured over with the seasoning in a pan.
Dormice: with pork forcemeat, likewise with flesh — from every limb of the dormice — ground with pepper, pine kernels, laser, fish-sauce, stuff the dormice and, sewn up, put them on a tile, set them in the oven, or, stuffed, cook them in an oven-dish.
Here begins the Sea-Book of Apicius Caelius.
IX.
Sauce for Lobster and Capers: firm chopped spring onion and a sauce: pepper, lovage, caraway, cumin, date, honey, vinegar, wine, fish-sauce, oil, reduced must. Add mustard quickly to the boiled dishes.
Roasted Lobsters you will make thus: the lobsters are opened, as is usual, with their shell, and there is poured over them a peppered, coriander sauce, and so they are roasted on a gridiron. When they have dried, you add to them, on the gridiron, as often as they dry, until they are roasted.
Boiled lobster with cumin-sauce you will serve well: pepper, lovage, parsley, dry mint, rather more cumin, honey, vinegar, fish-sauce; if you wish, you will add spikenard leaf and malabathrum.
Otherwise, Lobster: forcemeats of its tail you will make thus: first take off the husk, then boil the flesh, chop it, and with fish-sauce, pepper, and eggs shape the forcemeats.
For Boiled Lobster: pepper, cumin, rue, honey, vinegar, fish-sauce, and oil.
Otherwise, for Lobster: pepper, lovage, cumin, mint, rue, pine kernels, honey, vinegar, fish-sauce, and wine.

title: De Re Coquinaria
text:
For Electric-Ray: pound pepper, rue, dried spring onion, honey, fish-sauce, raisin-wine, a little wine, drops of good oil. When it begins to boil, bind with starch.
For Boiled Electric-Ray: pepper, lovage, parsley, mint, oregano, the middle of an egg, honey, fish-sauce, raisin-wine, wine, oil; if you wish, add mustard, vinegar; if you want it fish-pickled, add raisins.
For Squid in a Pan: pound pepper, rue, a little honey, fish-sauce, boiled must, drops of oil. For Stuffed Squid: pepper, lovage, coriander, celery seed, egg yolk, honey, vinegar, fish-sauce, wine, and oil. Bind it.
For Stuffed Cuttlefish: pepper, lovage, celery seed, caraway, honey, fish-sauce, wine, basket-seasonings. Heat it, and so open the cuttlefish and pour it over.
You will make a Cooked Cuttlefish thus: pound boiled de-nerved brains with pepper, into which you mix enough raw eggs, whole pepper, small forcemeats, and so consume it and put it into a boiling pot so that the stuffing can come together.
Cuttlefish boiled, put from the cauldron into cold water, with pepper, laser, fish-sauce, pine kernels, eggs; and season it as you wish.
Otherwise, Cuttlefish: pepper, lovage, cumin, green coriander, dry mint, egg yolk, honey, fish-sauce, wine, vinegar, and oil; and when it has boiled, bind with starch.
For Octopus: with pepper, fish-sauce, laser, serve it.
For Oysters: pepper, lovage, egg yolk, vinegar, fish-sauce, oil, and wine. If you wish, add honey too.
For Every Kind of Shellfish: pepper, lovage, parsley, dry mint, rather more cumin, honey, fish-sauce; if you wish, spikenard leaf and malabathrum.
For Sea-Urchin: take a new saucepan, a little oil, fish-sauce, sweet wine, ground pepper. Make it boil; when it has boiled, put it into the individual urchins, stir, let it boil three times. When you have cooked it, scatter pepper and serve.
Otherwise, for Sea-Urchin: pepper, a little costmary, dry mint, honey-wine, fish-sauce, Indian spikenard, and spikenard leaf.
Otherwise, for Sea-Urchin: put it in a colander, cook it in hot water. Lift it, arrange it in a pan, add spikenard leaf, pepper, honey, fish-sauce, a little oil, eggs, and so bind it; cook it on warm ashes, scatter pepper, and serve.
For Salted Sea-Urchin: temper salted sea-urchin with the best fish-sauce, boiled must, pepper, and set it out.
Otherwise: mix salted sea-urchins with the best fish-sauce, and everyone will think them all fresh, so that they could be taken straight from the bath.
For Mussels: fish-sauce, chopped leek, cumin, raisin-wine, savory, wine; make the mixture more watery and cook the mussels in it.
For Sardines. A stuffed sardine ought to be made thus: the sardine is boned. There is heated pennyroyal, cumin, grains of pepper, mint, walnuts, honey. It is filled and sewn up, wrapped in paper, and so set over the steam of the fire in a covered dish. It is seasoned with oil, boiled must, fish-pickle.
A Sardine is made thus: the sardine is cooked and boned. Pepper is ground with lovage, thyme, oregano, rue, date, honey, and in a little vessel the stuffing is garnished with chopped eggs. A little wine, vinegar, reduced must, and green oil.
Sauce for Sardine: pepper, oregano, onion, a little vinegar, and oil.
Sauce for Sardine: pepper, lovage, dry mint, onion, cooked honey, vinegar, oil. Pour it over, and scatter with chopped hard eggs.
Sauce for Sardine: pepper, lovage, celery seed, mint, rue, date, honey, vinegar, wine, and oil.
The sauce used for grey mullet suits the sardine too.
Sauce for Salted Grey Mullet: pepper, lovage, cumin, onion, rue, garden-herb, date, honey, vinegar, mustard, and oil.

title: De Re Coquinaria
text:
Otherwise, Sauce for Salted Grey Mullet: pepper, oregano, rocket, mint, rue, garden-herb, date, honey, oil, vinegar, and mustard.
Sauce for Salted Sheatfish, Bonito, and Tunny: pepper, lovage, cumin, onion, mint, rue, garden-herb, date, honey, vinegar, mustard, oil.
Sauce for Salted Red Mullet: pepper, rue, onion, date, mustard, mix it ground with sea-urchin and oil, and so pour it over the fried or roasted fish.
Salt-Fish without Salt-Fish: cook liver, pound it, and put in peppered fish-sauce or salt, add oil, hare's or kid's or lamb's or chicken's liver, and if you wish, shape a fish in a little mould. Add green oil over the top.
Otherwise, in Place of Salt-Fish: cumin, pepper, fish-sauce, pound them, and a little raisin-wine or boiled must, and mix in very many ground walnuts, and pound together, and pour into a salt-dish, drip a little oil over the top, and serve.
Otherwise, Salt-Fish without Salt-Fish: as much cumin as you can take up with five fingers, pepper to half of it, and grapes; pound a clove of cleaned garlic, pour fish-sauce over, drip a little oil over the top. This greatly refreshes an ailing stomach and aids digestion.
Baian Stew: put into a pot small oysters, sea-urchin spines, sea-nettles, roasted chopped pine kernels, rue, celery, pepper, coriander, cumin, raisin-wine, fish-sauce, date, oil.
Here begins the Fisherman's Offering of Apicius Caelius.
X.
Herb-Sauce for Fried Fish: clean whatever fish you wish, salt it, fry it. Pound pepper, cumin, coriander seed, laser root, oregano, rue, work it, moisten with vinegar, add date, honey, reduced must, oil, fish-sauce, temper. Pour it back into a pot. Make it boil. When it has boiled, pour over the fried fish, scatter pepper, and serve.
Sauce for Boiled Fish: pepper, lovage, cumin, spring onion, oregano, pine kernels, date, honey, vinegar, fish-sauce, mustard, a little oil. If you wish a fish-pickle sauce, raisins.
Otherwise, for Boiled Fish: pound pepper, lovage, green coriander, savory, onion, two cooked egg yolks, raisin-wine, vinegar, oil, and fish-sauce.
Otherwise, Sauce for Boiled Fish: clean the fish carefully. Put into a mortar salt, coriander seed, pound them, in which roll it, put it into a pan, cover it, seal it with plaster, cook it in the oven. When it is cooked, take it out. Sprinkle it with the sharpest vinegar and serve.
Otherwise, Sauce for Boiled Fish: when you have cleaned the fish, put into a frying-pan seed, water, green dill, and the fish itself. When it is cooked, sprinkle with vinegar and serve.
Alexandrian Sauce for Roasted Fish: pepper, dried onion, lovage, cumin, oregano, celery seed, stoned damsons, must-cake, fish-sauce, reduced must, oil, and cook it.
Otherwise, Alexandrian Sauce for Roasted Fish: pepper, lovage, green coriander, stoned raisins, wine, fish-sauce, oil, and cook it.
Otherwise, Alexandrian Sauce for Roasted Fish: pepper, lovage, green coriander, onion, stoned damsons, raisin-wine, fish-sauce, vinegar, oil, and cook it.
Sauce for Roasted Conger: pepper, lovage, fried cumin, oregano, dried onion, cooked egg yolks, wine, honey-wine, vinegar, fish-sauce, reduced must, and cook it.
Sauce for Horned-Fish: pepper, lovage, oregano, onion, stoned raisins, wine, honey, vinegar, fish-sauce, oil, and cook it.
Sauce for Roasted Red Mullet: pepper, lovage, rue, honey, pine kernels, vinegar, wine, fish-sauce, a little oil. Heat it and pour over.
Otherwise, Sauce for Roasted Red Mullet: rue, mint, coriander, fennel, all green, pepper, lovage, honey, fish-sauce, and a little oil.

title: De Re Coquinaria
text:
Sauce for Roasted Bonito: pepper, lovage, oregano, green coriander, onion, stoned raisins, vinegar, fish-sauce, reduced must, oil, and cook it. This sauce suits the boiled fish too. If you wish, add honey.
Sauce for Perch: pepper, lovage, fried cumin, onion, stoned damsons, wine, honey-wine, vinegar, oil, reduced must, and cook it.
Sauce for Red Sea-Bream: pepper, lovage, caraway, wild thyme, celery seed, dried onion, wine, raisin-wine, vinegar, fish-sauce, oil. Bind with starch.
Sauce for Roasted Lamprey: pepper, lovage, savory, saffron-paste, onion, stoned damsons, wine, honey-wine, vinegar, fish-sauce, reduced must, oil, and cook it.
Otherwise, Sauce for Roasted Lamprey: pepper, lovage, damsons, wine, honey-wine, vinegar, fish-sauce, reduced must, oil, and cook it.
Otherwise, Sauce for Roasted Lamprey: pepper, lovage, mountain catmint, coriander seed, onion, pine kernels, honey, vinegar, fish-sauce, oil, and cook it.
Otherwise, Sauce for Roasted Lamprey: pepper, lovage, dill, celery seed, Syrian sumac, date, honey, vinegar, fish-sauce, oil, mustard, reduced must.
Otherwise, Sauce for Boiled Lamprey: pepper, lovage, caraway, celery seed, coriander, dry mint, pine kernels, rue, honey, vinegar, wine, fish-sauce, a little oil. Heat it and bind with starch.
Otherwise, Sauce for Boiled Lamprey: pepper, lovage, caraway, cumin, pine kernels, date, mustard, honey, vinegar, fish-sauce, oil, reduced must.
Sauce for Boiled Fish: pepper, lovage, parsley, oregano, dried onion, honey, vinegar, fish-sauce, wine, a little oil. When it has boiled, bind with starch and serve on a platter.
Sauce for Boiled Horse-Mackerel: pepper, lovage, cumin, green rue, onion, honey, vinegar, fish-sauce, a little oil. When it has boiled, bind with starch.
Sauce for Roasted Fish: pepper, lovage, thyme, green coriander, honey, vinegar, fish-sauce, wine, oil, reduced must. Heat it and stir with a sprig of rue and bind with starch.
Sauce for Tunny: pepper, cumin, thyme, coriander, onion, raisins, vinegar, honey, wine, fish-sauce, oil. Heat it and bind with starch.
Sauce for Boiled Tunny: pepper, lovage, thyme, condiment, garden-herb, onion, date, honey, vinegar, fish-sauce and oil and mustard.
Sauce for Roasted Dentex: pepper, lovage, coriander, mint, dry rue, quince, cooked honey, wine, fish-sauce, oil. Heat it and bind with starch.
Sauce for Boiled Dentex: pepper, dill, cumin, thyme, mint, green rue, honey, vinegar, fish-sauce, wine, a little oil. Heat it and bind with starch.
Sauce for Gilt-Head Bream: pepper, lovage, caraway, oregano, a rue berry, mint, a myrtle berry, egg yolk, honey, vinegar, oil, wine, fish-sauce. Heat it and so use it.
Sauce for Roasted Gilt-Head Bream: pepper, coriander, dry mint, celery seed, onion, raisins, honey, vinegar, wine, fish-sauce, oil.
Sauce for Boiled Scorpion-Fish: pepper, caraway, parsley, date, honey, vinegar, fish-sauce, mustard, oil, reduced must.
For Fish in Wine-and-Fish-Sauce: pound pepper, rue, honey, mix in raisin-wine, fish-sauce, boiled must, and heat it over a very gentle fire. Otherwise, for Fish in Wine-and-Fish-Sauce: make it as above. When it has boiled, bind with starch.
Sauce for Eel: pepper, lovage, celery seed, dill, Syrian sumac, date, honey, vinegar, fish-sauce, oil, mustard, and reduced must.
Sauce for Eel: pepper, lovage, Syrian sumac, dry mint, rue berries, cooked egg yolks, honey-wine, vinegar, fish-sauce, oil. Cook it.
